{\LARGE\bfseries Sonne: automated installation}\par
\textbf{You need:} Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Debian 13, approximately 8 GiB RAM,
15 GiB free disk, internet access and a user account with sudo.

\step{Create the application and copy its ID}
Open \href{https://discord.com/developers/applications}{Discord Developer Portal}.
Choose \textbf{Create / New Application}, name it \textbf{Sonne} and create it.
In \textbf{General Information}, copy your \textbf{Application ID}.

\step{Copy the token and enable message content}
On \textbf{Bot}, copy the token and keep it for the installer.
Use \textbf{Reset Token} only if needed; it invalidates the previous token.
Enable \textbf{Message Content Intent}; leave Presence and Server Members off.
\begin{center}\shotIntent\end{center}
\captionline{Figure 4. Enable Message Content Intent.}

\step{Select scopes, permissions and invite the bot}
Open \textbf{OAuth2 / URL Generator}. Select \texttt{bot} and
\texttt{applications.commands}. Grant \textbf{View Channels, Send Messages,
Read Message History, Embed Links} and \textbf{Attach Files}; keep Administrator off.
Open the generated invitation URL, choose your server and authorize the bot.
Create a text channel named \texttt{sonne}, accessible to the bot and intended users.
\begin{center}\shotScopes\end{center}
\captionline{Figure 5. Select only bot and applications.commands.}

\newpage
\pageheading{Copy IDs and run the installer}
\step{Enable Developer Mode and copy the IDs}
In Discord, open \textbf{User Settings / Advanced} and enable \textbf{Developer Mode}.
\begin{center}\shotDeveloper\end{center}
\captionline{Figure 6. Enable Developer Mode.}
Right-click the \textbf{server icon}, the chosen \textbf{text channel} and each
\textbf{allowed user}. Copy the respective numeric ID.
\begin{center}
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.37\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}\centering
\shotServer
\captionline{Figure 7. Copy Server ID.}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.32\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}\centering
\shotChannel
\captionline{Figure 8. Copy Channel ID.}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.22\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}\centering
\shotUser
\captionline{Figure 9. Copy User ID.}
\end{minipage}
\end{center}
Use your own IDs; these screenshots show examples.

\step{Download and run the installer}
In the Ubuntu or Debian terminal, clone the repository and run the installer
as your normal user:
\begin{lstlisting}
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y git
git clone https://github.com/Krabbens/sonne.git ~/sonne-installer
cd ~/sonne-installer
bash scripts/install-sonne.sh
\end{lstlisting}
Enter your sudo password when requested. At the prompts, enter:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Bot token (hidden while typing).
\item Application ID.
\item Server ID.
\item Channel ID.
\item Allowed User IDs, separated by commas.
\end{enumerate}
Wait for the installer to finish. If a download is interrupted, run the same command again.

\newpage
\pageheading{Check that the bot works}
\step{Send a message}
In the allowed channel, from an allowed account, mention the bot:
\begin{lstlisting}
@Sonne Reply with exactly: sonne-ok
\end{lstlisting}
Wait for a visible reply; the first request can be slow.
\begin{center}\shotReply\end{center}
\captionline{Figure 10. Example reply from the running bot.}

\step{Test an image and a file}
Attach \texttt{examples/vision-check.png} from \texttt{\textasciitilde/agents/sonne}.
Ask the bot to read the large label and identify the red shape.
Expect \textbf{SONNE 42} and a \textbf{red square}.

Then ask it to create and read a new test file:
\begin{lstlisting}
@Sonne Create files/smoke.txt containing exactly SONNE FILE OK.
Read it back.
\end{lstlisting}
In the Linux terminal, verify the saved file:
\begin{lstlisting}
cd ~/agents/sonne
cat workspace/files/smoke.txt
\end{lstlisting}

\step{If the bot does not reply}
Check the token, IDs, channel permissions and Message Content Intent.
In the Linux terminal, inspect service status and recent logs:
\begin{lstlisting}
cd ~/agents/sonne
docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail=100 openclaw
\end{lstlisting}
If Docker reports a permission error, log out of Linux and log back in.
